link-judge.copiedFrom: originally dissert/wiki/notes/prompts.md § Document entities streaming linking judge (Ψ_link) (replaced the pre-redesign two-verdict prompt 2026-08-04); diverged 2026-08-17 — the repo copy is now the source of truth
link-judge.note: 2026-08-22: ladder/rung vocabulary removed for the SKOS graph branch — mentions carry no mentionRung and candidates render no rung; hierarchy is expressed only as parentCandidate + edgeKind. 2026-08-17: made domain-neutral. Structured roles are never rendered; source context may establish only explicit naming identity, not identity from behavior or relationships.

variables.source: first 600 chars of the source document, whitespace-collapsed
numbered unresolved mentions with candidate sets (canonical, rung, aliases)

listwise-graph-v2.note: 2026-08-20: v1 plus the document-scoped parent pool. Parents are chosen by P-number from every entity the source put on the table, because 14 of 24 reachable gold edges had a parent the identity blocker never retrieved at any depth.

listwise-select-compact-v1.note: 2026-08-18 prompt-optimization arm: compact positional output, explicit completeness, and identity-bearing identifier/version guards.

listwise-skos-v1.note: 2026-08-22: listwise-graph-compact-v8 restated as a strict SKOS ballot — the Levels/`lvl` field (ladder) is gone, and `r` gains `b` (the mention is BROADER than the listed entity; the edge is stored reversed, listed->mention). Identity = skos:exactMatch (alias), `v`/`n`/`p` = the mention is the narrower side, kept trinary so the stored `relation` survives for kind agreement and contract folds.

listwise-skos-v2.note: 2026-08-22: listwise-skos-v1 with word-valued relation codes (version|narrower|part|broader instead of v|n|p|b) — the ablation isolating whether single-letter codes cost relation-type accuracy. Rules and ballot structure byte-identical to v1.

listwise-skos-v3.note: 2026-08-22: listwise-skos-v1 with rule 2 reframed after the catch-up diagnosis — hierarchy is answered from general knowledge (the source need not state it), `p` explicitly scans the whole E-list rather than the mention's options row (doc 3028: the judge only ever asserted parents that sat inside options), and a run of sibling derivatives under one listed base is named as the common case. Identity rules byte-identical to v1.

listwise-skos-v4.note: 2026-08-22: the set-level ablation — hierarchy moves out of the per-mention row into a top-level `e` edge list judged over the whole E-list after identity, mirroring the catch-up ballot's registry-review framing inside the per-document call. Per-mention `p`/`r` are gone; the parser maps each edge back onto the decision of the mention it anchors.

listwise-skos-v5.note: 2026-08-22: v3 with the gloss moved BEFORE the hierarchy answer — section order and output key order both `m,id,g,p,r`. Motivated by the reverse-order 3028 transcript: the judge wrote 'Chromium-based web browser' as the gloss of 15 mentions while answering p:null on each — the knowledge arrives after the decision it should inform. Adds the explicit contradiction rule: a gloss saying 'X-based'/'component of X' with p:null is inconsistent.

listwise-skos-v6.note: 2026-08-22: v5 plus the `kin:` rule for DOC_SIBLINGS_MODE=kin — each mention's row may carry the E numbers of its embedding-nearest co-mentions as candidate relatives (never identity options; a sibling is not the parent, the shared base is). Splits the doc-sibling mechanism from the identity row after the options-mode ablation cost the shellcode.x64.bin identity link.

listwise-skos-v7.note: 2026-08-22: v5 plus the vulnerability-identifier rule — a CVE/advisory/exploit identifier is not narrower than the product it affects (a flaw lives IN a product without being a kind, version, or part of it). Motivated by the REASK_CARRY arms: 14 of 26 non-gold edges were CVE-…→product placements once carried CVE orphans were re-asked under the scan-the-E-list epistemics.

listwise-id-v1.note: 2026-08-23: pass-1 prompt of the decoupled v8 architecture — identity + gloss ONLY (v7's identity rules verbatim, hierarchy explicitly out of scope), JSONL output (one object per line; a truncated ballot loses a suffix, not everything). Hierarchy lives in the source-free pass-2 review call. Motivated by the frame finding (small judge refuses knowledge edges in the document frame) and the JSONL transport probes (73/73 rows recovered where nested JSON truncated).

repair-judge.copiedFrom: originally dissert/wiki/notes/prompts.md § Suspect-component repair judge (Ψ_repair) — new prompt for the synchronous StreamingRepairer (T2), replacing the deleted deferred RegistryConsolidator in the main pipeline; diverged 2026-08-17 — the repo copy is now the source of truth
repair-judge.note: 2026-08-17 amendment: the op-schema line documented `distinct{pair:[A,B]}`, whose A/B metavariables collide with the A./B./C. labels the component listing uses for readability. Measured on the Country probe (run 2026-08-17-country-probe-f7231e6e58e9): gemma4:e2b-16k answered `"pair": ["A","C"]` and ALL 17 repair calls were rejected as `unlisted-entity`, so repair could correct nothing on that model. The slot is now spelled `["<canonical name>","<canonical name>"]` with an explicit never-use-the-letter rule. StreamingRepairer additionally accepts a bare label as a fallback (name match takes precedence). This rotates every runId that includes this prompt.

variables.source: numbered suspect-component blocks: triggering signal(s) with scores (union-blocker / gloss-ANN / defer / coherence) and, per entity, canonical name, category, rung, aliases, gloss, minting document, and evidence snippets

repair-judge-compact-v1.note: 2026-08-18 prompt-optimization arm: compact schema, complete pair coverage, forbidden signal-as-op labels, and high-confidence explicit-identity merges only.
